message.content:
**Short answer** `docker start` is *not* the command to turn the Docker Engine on; it starts an **existing container**. To bring the Docker service up on Windows you need to start the **Docker Desktop** application (or the underlying Windows service). Below are the most common ways to do it from the command line: | Method | What it does | How to run | |--------|--------------|------------| | **PowerShell – Start the Docker Desktop service** | Starts the Windows service that runs the Docker Engine (`com.docker.service`). | ```powershell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
``` | | **Command Prompt – Start the Docker Desktop service** | Same as above but using the classic `sc` command. | ```cmd
sc start com.docker.service
``` | | **Launch Docker Desktop executable directly** | Opens the Docker Desktop GUI, which automatically starts the engine. | ```powershell
& "$env:ProgramFiles\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"
``` | | **Use Docker Desktop’s “Start” button** | If you prefer a GUI, just click the “Start” button in the Docker Desktop tray icon. | (No command needed) | --- ### Why `docker start` isn’t what you’re looking for - `docker start ` starts a **container** that has already been created and stopped. - It requires the Docker Engine to be running already. - It will *not* bring the Docker Engine itself up if it’s stopped. --- ### Step‑by‑step guide 1. **Open PowerShell as Administrator** - Press `Win + X`, choose “Windows PowerShell (Admin)” (or “Windows Terminal (Admin)” if you’re on newer Windows 10/11). - If you’re using the classic Command Prompt, open it as Administrator instead. 2. **Start the Docker service** ```powershell Start-Service -Name com.docker.service ``` *or* ```cmd sc start com.docker.service ``` 3. **Verify the service is running** ```powershell Get-Service -Name com.docker.service ``` You should see `Status : Running`. 4. **(Optional) Verify Docker CLI works** ```powershell docker version ``` This should return the client and server versions, confirming the engine is up. --- ### Using the Docker Desktop GUI If you prefer a graphical interface: 1. Click the Docker Desktop icon in the system tray (bottom right corner). 2. If it’s not already running, you’ll see a “Start” button. Click it. 3. Once the Docker Desktop window opens, the engine is running in the background. --- ### Quick one‑liner (if you want to run it from a script) ```powershell Start-Service -Name com.docker.service ``` or, if you’re in a batch file: ```batch sc start com.docker.service ``` --- #### Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | “Access denied” when running `Start-Service` | Run PowerShell/Command Prompt **as Administrator**. | | Service name wrong | Verify the service name: `Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -like "*Docker*"}` | | Docker Desktop not installed | Install Docker Desktop from https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop | --- ### TL;DR - **`docker start` → starts a container.** - **To start Docker itself on Windows:** ```powershell Start-Service -Name com.docker.service ``` or ```cmd sc start com.docker.service ``` That will bring the Docker Engine up and ready for you to run `docker run`, `docker ps`, etc.
